Class BaseContainer

java.lang.Object
java.awt.Component
java.awt.Container
javax.swing.JComponent
edu.cnu.mdi.container.BaseContainer
All Implemented Interfaces:
IContainer, HoverListener, ItemChangeListener, ImageObserver, MenuContainer, Serializable, EventListener
Direct Known Subclasses:
MapContainer
public class BaseContainer extends JComponent implements IContainer, ItemChangeListener, HoverListener
Primary 2D drawing container for MDI.

A container holds a world-coordinate viewport and a z-stack of Layers. Each layer holds a collection of AItems.

Layer architecture

This container defines three standard layers:
  • Connections (protected; drawn first / bottom)
  • Content (default user layer; typical items go here)
  • Annotations (protected; drawn last / top)

Important implementation note

Layer's constructor auto-registers the new layer with the container via IContainer.addLayer(Layer). During this container's constructor, the protected layer fields are not yet assigned when the first addLayer calls occur.

Therefore, after constructing the layers we explicitly remove the protected layers from _layers and re-add the default user layer if needed. This guarantees that:

  • _layers contains only user layers
  • protected layers are still drawn and hit-tested in their fixed positions

Visibility and locking

Container-wide operations that involve user interaction (hit testing, selection, deletion, enclosed selection) respect:
  • Layer.isVisible() — invisible layers are ignored for hit testing and enclosure
  • Layer.isLocked() — locked layers are treated as non-interactive and ignored

Tool handler extensibility

Subclasses that need a specialised BaseToolHandler should override createToolHandler() rather than overriding setToolBar(AToolBar). This keeps the base class free of instanceof checks against specific subclasses.

File drag-and-drop

Drop support is no longer installed here. It is managed centrally by BaseView.enableFileDrop(), which attaches a single FileDropHandler to the canvas component (this object), the scroll-pane viewport (when present), and the view frame itself. Subclasses of BaseView activate drop support with one call:

    enableFileDrop(myFileFilter);   // in the BaseView subclass constructor

    • setView

      public void setView(BaseView view)
      Associate this container with its hosting view.

      File drag-and-drop wiring is not done here; it is the responsibility of the view itself via BaseView.enableFileDrop(java.util.function.Predicate). This keeps all drop-surface management in one place and avoids the container needing to know about the transfer layer.

      Set the container's view.
      Specified by:
      setView in interface IContainer
      Parameters:
      view - the view to set.

    • itemChanged

      public void itemChanged(Layer layer, AItem item, ItemChangeType type)
      Responds to item change events fired by layers owned by this container.

      The base implementation:

      • Updates the toolbar state (e.g. enables/disables the delete button) when an item is selected or deselected.
      • Marks the affected item dirty on any change, triggering a repaint on the next refresh() call.
      All other change types are no-ops in the base class. Subclasses may override to add behaviour for specific types such as MOVED or DELETED.
      Specified by:
      itemChanged in interface ItemChangeListener
      Parameters:
      layer - the layer containing the changed item
      item - the affected item; may be null for layer-level events
      type - the type of change

    • getWorldSystem

      public Rectangle2D.Double getWorldSystem()
      Get the current world system.

      Note: implementations may return the live, mutable rectangle backing the container's viewport, not a defensive copy (unlike IContainer.setWorldSystem(Rectangle2D.Double) and resetWorldSystem, which both copy). Mutating the returned rectangle directly can silently change the container's viewport without going through setDirty/ refresh. Callers that need to keep a stable snapshot should copy it themselves.

      Specified by:
      getWorldSystem in interface IContainer
      Returns:
      the world system; may be the container's live instance
